findings.mechanism: The supplied QAC function gives mā the local relative role, while its contact with illā keeps a second restriction-shaped route perceptible without displacing that role.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel why the clause is grammatically precise and theologically forceful at once.
findings.containment: The two pressures coexist; the finding does not select one as the only valid reading.

epistemic.reason: The candidate evidence marks the relative parse as local and the negative route as narrowed pressure.

findings.title: ongoing worship practice
findings.claim: The imperfect indicative presents the people's worship as an ongoing communal practice inside the exception frame.
findings.mechanism: The Form I imperfect and plural ending keep the action ongoing, while mā and illā route it into the clause's object-and-exception structure.
findings.reader_payoff: The youths are separating from a living practice, not merely from a past claim.
findings.containment: The finding stays with the supplied worship/service reading and its local syntax.

epistemic.reason: Mood, aspect, number, and particle-frame evidence are explicit.

findings.title: worship with submission pressure
findings.claim: The ordinary worship action carries a bounded pressure of service, humility, and subjection.
findings.mechanism: The ʿ-b-d root supplies the submission field, while the local imperfect form and exception syntax keep the event as ongoing communal worship rather than a separate slavery meaning.
findings.reader_payoff: Worship is felt as a binding relation of practiced submission.
findings.containment: Submission colors the selected worship act; it does not replace it with legal servitude.

epistemic.reason: The candidate evidence explicitly narrows the wider root family to the local Form I action.

findings.title: worship becomes a boundary
findings.claim: The ongoing worship verb turns the preceding false-god accusation into a named practice from which the youths withdraw.
findings.mechanism: The verb supplies the living devotional act, and the supported boundary echoes let that act carry forward into a monotheistic limit within the local sequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The boundary is directed against an actual practice, not an abstract label.
findings.containment: The echo remains attached to the local verb and does not make a later formula the subject of this ayah.

epistemic.reason: The candidate supplies used local and same-surah boundary evidence.

findings.title: exception pivot
findings.claim: The exception particle pivots the worship phrase toward the named divine exception.
findings.mechanism: Illā assigns the following proper name its exception role and makes the clause turn from the worship field to the one retained referent.
findings.reader_payoff: Exclusivity is carried by the syntax of the clause, not only by a theological word choice.
findings.containment: The finding describes the particle's local exception function and leaves the supplied variant contrast separate.

epistemic.reason: Particle government and exception role are directly supplied.

findings.title: exclusion variant pressure
findings.claim: Variant exclusion frames expose nearby shifts in stance while the canonical wording keeps exception grammar central.
findings.mechanism: The canonical illā construction carries the local pivot, and the supplied variant readings make the force of alternative exclusion frames perceptible by contrast.
findings.reader_payoff: The exact wording of the boundary gains weight without losing the main parse.
findings.containment: Variants remain contrastive evidence and do not replace the canonical exception.

epistemic.reason: The candidate record explicitly narrows accepted variant evidence to contrast.

findings.title: named exception toward guidance
findings.claim: The proper divine name closes the worship exception and carries a local contact toward guidance agency in the cave sequence.
findings.mechanism: The name first functions as the accusative exception, then the supplied same-surah thread lets the same named referent remain active as the cave scene turns toward guidance.
findings.reader_payoff: The name links the boundary they defend to the care that follows it.
findings.containment: The finding tracks a same-sequence contact; it does not import a surah-wide thesis.

epistemic.reason: Proper-name evidence and the supplied same-surah thread are both used.

findings.title: named accusative exception
findings.claim: The exception is anchored in a proper divine name with a visible accusative role.
findings.mechanism: Illā governs the accusative name, so the clause retains one explicitly named referent rather than an open category of deities.
findings.reader_payoff: The exception becomes grammatically and referentially precise.
findings.containment: The claim concerns this name's local case and exception role, not every derivational pressure in its root family.

epistemic.reason: Proper-name form, case, and particle government are directly supported.

findings.title: refuge pressure at the divine name
findings.claim: The divine name carries bounded refuge-orientation pressure as the next movement turns toward shelter.
findings.mechanism: The name is the carrier, and the following refuge command is the independent contact that lets worship-orientation and seeking refuge touch while the accusative exception remains local.
findings.reader_payoff: The name's exception role opens naturally into the act of seeking refuge.
findings.containment: Refuge is a qualified derivational pressure, not a replacement gloss for the proper name.

epistemic.reason: The candidate evidence explicitly narrows derivational and refuge pressure by the local exception construction.

findings.title: boundary into command
findings.claim: The resultative fāʾ turns the completed withdrawal boundary into the cave command.
findings.mechanism: The particle follows the framed separation and makes refuge its consequence, shifting the ayah from diagnosis to directed movement.
findings.reader_payoff: The command feels causally released by the boundary just stated.
findings.containment: The result relation connects these local clauses; it does not make later imperative echoes part of the local grammar.

epistemic.reason: The supplied local analysis and echo evidence support the consequence hinge.

findings.title: result-command hinge
findings.claim: Cave refuge is presented as the practical result of the completed withdrawal condition.
findings.mechanism: The resultative particle and framed clause join separation to the imperative, so the cave is the next action generated by the condition already described.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah's movement from refusal to refuge becomes one continuous turn.
findings.containment: The hinge preserves both the withdrawal and the command; neither clause absorbs the other.

epistemic.reason: Resultative syntax, frame, and command evidence are directly supplied.

findings.title: attributed transfer into expansion
findings.claim: The focus sequence can be read as transfer out of one field of attachment into gathered refuge, where enclosure becomes a site of unfolding.
findings.mechanism: The attributed trace pairs withdrawal from people and worship with joining refuge, cave protection, and spreading; the distinct focus words contact one another and change bare hiding into protected movement with expansion.
findings.reader_payoff: The cave is newly perceptible as a gathered refuge whose enclosure enables opening outward.
findings.containment: This remains an attributed contextual reading of the exact focus trace; the ordinary withdrawal, cave, and spreading reading stays intact.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace has exact focus coordinates and complete anchor scope, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound.
